related_questions.question: What does the COVID vaccine do to your body?

text_blocks.snippet: COVID-19 vaccines work by training your immune system to recognize and fight the virus without causing a severe illness. They introduce a harmless piece of the virus (like a protein) to your body, prompting your immune system to produce antibodies and other protective cells. This process allows your body to develop immunity, so if you encounter the real virus later, your immune system is already prepared to neutralize it.
snippet_highlighted_words: training your immune system to recognize and fight the virus without causing a severe illness

list.title: 1. Introduction of Viral Component:
list.snippet: The vaccine delivers a piece of the COVID-19 virus, such as the spike protein, into your body.

list.title: 2. Immune System Response:
list.snippet: Your immune system recognizes this viral component as foreign and begins to produce antibodies and activate other immune cells.

list.title: 3. Immunity Development:
list.snippet: This response prepares your body to fight off future infections with the actual COVID-19 virus.

list.title: 4. Learning and Protection:
list.snippet: The vaccine teaches your body to recognize the virus and mount a defense, providing protection against severe illness, hospitalization, and death.

list.title: 5. Building Protection:
list.snippet: Side effects from the vaccine, like soreness at the injection site or mild fever, are normal signs that your body is building immunity.

text_blocks.snippet: Common side effects of COVID-19 vaccines are typically mild and short-lived, including pain, soreness, redness, or swelling at the injection site, fatigue, headache, muscle pain, joint pain, chills, fever, and nausea or vomiting. These side effects are generally mild and resolve on their own within a few days.
snippet_highlighted_words: pain, soreness, redness, or swelling at the injection site, fatigue, headache, muscle pain, joint pain, chills, fever, and nausea or vomiting

list.title: Injection Site Reactions:
list.snippet: Pain, soreness, redness, or swelling at the injection site are frequently reported.

list.title: Systemic Symptoms:
list.snippet: Fatigue, headache, muscle pain, joint pain, chills, fever, and nausea or vomiting can occur.

list.title: Infants and Toddlers:
list.snippet: Common symptoms in this age group may include irritability, crying, decreased appetite, and sleepiness.

text_blocks.snippet: Less Common, but Possible Side Effects:

list.title: Allergic Reactions:
list.snippet: Although rare, severe allergic reactions (anaphylaxis) can occur after vaccination. This is why individuals are monitored for at least 15 minutes after vaccination (and 30 minutes for those with a history of non-severe allergic reactions to COVID-19 vaccines) according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention | CDC (.gov).

list.title: Myocarditis and Pericarditis:
list.snippet: These are rare inflammatory conditions of the heart muscle and lining, respectively. They have been reported, particularly in adolescents and young adults, after mRNA vaccines (Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna).

list.title: Thrombosis with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome (TTS):
list.snippet: This is a rare but serious condition involving blood clots and low platelet counts. It has been associated with the Johnson & Johnson (Janssen) vaccine.

list.title: Monitoring:
list.snippet: It is important to monitor for any side effects after vaccination and seek medical advice if needed.

list.title: Individual Variation:
list.snippet: Side effects can vary from person to person.

list.title: Severity:
list.snippet: While most side effects are mild, some can be more severe. The CDC recommends individuals to discuss any concerns about side effects with their healthcare provider.

list.title: Reporting:
list.snippet: Side effects can be reported to the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS).
